paragraphs: Issur shennitareb behetter, ap-al-gab demaran za"l pasaq besiman tzch, bemin baenu mino samekinan atteimat goy, beheka deeno yodea shessomekin alayv hamminhag pashut deen lismok al haggoy, ukemo shekkatab mvr"m za"l, veken hamminhag barur poh irenu bagdad y": ella meshaarin beshishshim ben nitareb min baenu mino, ben nitareb min bemino: vaapillu im yesh shishshim lebattel haasur im roin sheadayin taam haasur nirgash, kegon shehaissur mutam beyoter, hare zeh asur: vaayin "peri chadash", v"peri toar" seip qatan d.

clarification.explanation: When a forbidden food (such as milk that fell into meat) becomes mixed into a permitted food, although there is a rule of Maran (the Shulchan Aruch) that in a case of "a kind mixed with a different kind" (different types of food) one may rely on a gentile's tasting to know whether the forbidden taste is still noticeable, in practice this is not done where the gentile does not know he is being relied upon — and this is the accepted Baghdad custom. Instead, one always estimates by a sixty-fold quantity against the forbidden substance, whether it is "a kind mixed with a different kind" or "a kind mixed with its own kind." But even if there is sixty to nullify the forbidden substance, if the forbidden taste is nevertheless clearly and strongly noticeable (for example, if the forbidden substance was heavily spiced and flavorful), the mixture is still forbidden.
takeaways: One does not rely on a gentile's tasting to check nullification of a prohibition — one always estimates by a sixty-fold quantity, whether the same kind or a different kind.
Even with sixty, if the forbidden taste is still clearly noticeable (such as an especially spiced prohibition), the mixture remains forbidden.

paragraphs: Im haissur vehahetter shavim bemishqal, dehaynu shehem mimmin echad, sheen haechad kabed betibo yoter mechabero nukal leshaer bishnehem bimdida o bemishqal: abal im beechad yesh napucha vechalal yoter mechabero, en leshaer bimdida ella bemishqal, im shavin betiban, sheen echad mehem kabed betibo yoter mechabero, tzarik leshaer beomed umedida. velaken im napal chalab letok basar o lehepek, veken im napal kabed letok hattabshil hare ellu shavim betiban, umeshaarim bemishqal: abal im napal kap matteket shel chalab ben yomo letok tabshil shel basar o lehepek, en leshaer bemishqal, ki hammatteket kabed betibo kamma vekamma al basar umayim, ella meshaarim beomed ubekammut.veketzad yaaseh? hinneh minhagenu poh lishqol kap hammatteket, veim ala mea deraham, nachshob bachamishsha asar deraham, venatzrik sheyyihyeh battabshil shishshim peamim al chamishsha-asar deraham. ukepi mah shechaqarnu, tzarik lachshob keli hammatteket legabbe habbasar pachot min chamishsha-asar deraham lechumera. veayin "peri chadash", siman tzt,seip-qatan v, v"peri toar" sham, sop seip-qatan d, v"shiyyure-beraka" sham, ot b, v"minchat yeuddeh", kelal ph, seip qatan nch, v"chakemat-adam", kelal nb, ot g, veod acharonim. veayyen "bet-david", yoreh dea, siman mg, v"pitche-teshuba", siman tzch, seip qatan b. vekatab harab peri-toar", siman tzt sham, deim haasur vehahetter shavim bemishqal, kegon shehaissur basar belo atzamot, vehahetter gam-ken basar belo atzamot tob leshaer al-yede hammishqal, sheaz yatza hashshiur mekuvvan beyoter. vaayin "chinnuk bet yehuda" siman lg, v"abodat haggereshunni" siman l, v"matteh-yeuddeh" besop hasseper. veda ki haatzamot hem kebedim min habbasar, ukemo shekkatab b"shulchan gabohha", siman tzt, seip qatan y. veharab "bet-david", siman mg, hebi meharamba"m dehachittim kebedim min haqqemach echad mishsheyyashsheh, vehayyayin vehashshemen qallim min hammayim echad min esrim-veshiba:vekatab beshem rabbenu obadya za"l, dehen haggidin, hen haatzamot, hem kebedim min habbasar, ayin sham: abal hacheleb asher babbasar, hu shaveh im habbasar ukemo shekkatab b"shulchan gabohha".

clarification.explanation: When the forbidden and permitted substances are of similar nature (neither heavier nor more porous than the other), the ratio between them can be estimated by either volume or weight measurement. But if one is more porous or hollow than the other, one cannot estimate by volume, only by weight. If both are similar in nature, one may also estimate by visual judgment and measurement. For example, if milk fell into meat or vice versa, or if liver fell into a dish — they are similar in nature and are estimated by weight. But if a metal spoon that was "within its day" (used for milk that same day) fell into a meat dish or vice versa, one cannot estimate by weight, since metal is much heavier than meat or water. Instead, one estimates by judgment and quantity: for example, the custom is to weigh the metal spoon, and if it weighs one hundred dirhams, one estimates it absorbed a quantity of milk equal to about fifteen dirhams, and the dish must contain sixty times that quantity. And to be stringent, it is worthwhile to assume the spoon absorbed less than fifteen dirhams (so the sixty-fold requirement is sufficiently met). Bones are also heavier than meat, and sinews too are heavier than meat, and therefore they must be calculated separately; but milk absorbed within the meat itself is considered equal in weight to the meat.
takeaways: When the forbidden and permitted substances are similar in nature (such as meat and milk, or liver), one estimates the sixty-fold by weight or volume.
When there is a heavier object (like a metal spoon), one estimates by judgment of the absorbed quantity, not by its actual weight — and to be stringent, one assumes a smaller absorbed quantity.

paragraphs: Kap shel chalab ben yomo shehegisu bo biqdera shel basar al haesh im anachnu yodein kamma chalab bala zeh hakkap, kegon shehayeta kap chadasha, vehegisu bah kazzayit chalab bo bayyom shettechabo otah biqdera shel basar tzarik sheyyasim babbasar keneged kazzayit chalab, kevan dela yadeinan kamma bala hakkap min hechalab, baenan keneged kol kazzayit hacheleb. veken hu haddin im zo hakkap shel hechalab lo hayeta bat-yoma qodem shehegisu bah kazzayit hechalab, deaz kol mah shebbalea qodem hu lipgam, veachar shehegisu bah kazzayit hechalab, tachabu otah bebasar bo bayyom o tok meet leet deen tzarik leshaer ella keneged kazzayit hechalab lebattelo: abal im oto hakkap shel chalab hem megisim bah chalab roteach bekol yom, dela yadeinan kamma kazzayit cheleb balea, az tzarik leshaer keneged hakkap kullo: veraq im shel matteket, tzarik leshaer bekammut hakkap velo bemishqalo, veha al derek shekkatabnu leel, veken im hegisu chalab harbeh bakkap, dehaynu shehechalab haya mea deraham o yoter, vehakkap shel matteket asher kemoto, nechshab bachamishsha asar deraham o esrim deraham, veachar-kak tachabu zeh hakkap betabshil shel basar en tzarik shishshim ella keneged kammut hakkap shehu chamishsha-asar o esrim deraham, ki kevan dela yadeinan kamma bala, en lanu lomar shebbala yoter mishshiur kemoto, ella amerinan bala kekammuto, ubaenan sheyyasim keneged kemoto.

clarification.explanation: If a dairy spoon within its day (used for milk that same day) was used to stir a meat pot on the fire, and it is precisely known how much milk the spoon absorbed — for example, the spoon was new and was used to stir an olive's-measure of milk that same day — then sixty in the meat suffices against just that olive's-measure of milk, no more. Likewise, if the spoon was not within its day before being used for milk (whatever it absorbed earlier is now considered "spoiled" and does not count), and it was then used to stir a fresh olive's-measure of milk and immediately plunged into the meat, sixty against just that olive's-measure also suffices. But if the spoon is used daily to stir boiling milk and it is not known how much milk it has absorbed in total, one must estimate against the spoon's entire capacity — and if the spoon is metal, one estimates by the judged quantity (as mentioned in the previous halacha), not by its actual weight.
takeaways: A spoon whose absorbed milk quantity is precisely known (such as an olive's-measure) requires sixty only against that quantity.
A spoon used regularly for boiling milk with an unknown total absorption requires estimating against its entire capacity (by judgment, if metal).

paragraphs: Ha deamerinan detzarik leshaer keneged kol kemoto shel kap, haynu davqa im techabo hakkap bechalab shehaya mitbashshel lebaddo, deaz meshaarin shebbala hakkap min hechalab shiur kemoto, abal im haya hainyan kap: shehaya mebashshel baqqedera elep deraham mayim o shear roteb shel hatztzar, venapelu letokah mea deraham chalab, deaz niblelu hammayim vehechalab yachad, veachar kak tachab sham kap chadasha o enah bat-yoma betok haqqedera, ukemoto shel zeh hakkap oleh mea deraham ap-al-gab deamerinan shehakkap bala min haqqedera kashshiur kemoto shehu mea deraham, mikkol maqom zeh hammea deraham enam kullam chalab,ella hu leqacham mikkis hashshuttaput, dehaqqedera meorebet mayim vechalab, laken tzarik lachshob mah shemmaggia lekap min hechalab lepi cheshbon, veal zeh hacheleq hammaggia lo, tzarik shishshim lebattelo keshennapal achar-kak biqdera shel basar, vaayin lehaggaon chida" za"l b"shiyyure beraka", siman tzd, ot , mah shekkatab beshem mahara"sh amar za"l: vaayin "kanpe-yona", dap , ammud g, yeuyyan sham. umah shehiqsha harab "erek hashshulchan" za"l siman tzd, sop seip-qatan b al rabbenu chida" za"l, en zo qusheya, deharab "pene- aryeh za"l ayri betabshil gush sheppaga hakkap bechalab atzmo qodem shenniblal: umah shekkatab inyan "noten taam" ba lepalpel ulehasbir lashshoel dela shayyak beniddon didan hetter denoten – taam bar noten-taam: uleolam gam harab "pene-ryh"mvdh bedin zeh demahara"sh amar za"l, dei epshar lomar shebbala hakkap et hakkol, ella tzarik leshaer lepi cheshbon. veken shamati meharab ateret rashe mv"r abi zlh"h, shekkak haya moreh harab haggaon mv"r zeqeni rabbenu mosheh chayyim zlh"h bekamma inyanim leshaer lepi cheshbon, ukemo shekkatab mahara"sh za"l, veken anachnu nohagim atta. veim tishal: lamma lo naknis haqqedera atzmah shebbishshelu bah haroteb, shennapal betoko hechalab, name beshuttaput im haroteb, shennomar: keshem shellaqach haroteb min hechalab, kak laqecha haqqedera gam-ken lepi shiur kemotah? hinneh bedabar zeh heerakti harbeh besiyyata dishmayya besipre haqqadosh "rab-pealim" bitshuba, upilpalti bedibre happoseqim, ubearti hainyan heteb besiyyata dishmayya.

clarification.explanation:
The rule requiring estimation against the spoon's entire capacity applies specifically when it was plunged into milk cooked alone — where one then estimates the spoon absorbed milk equal to its full capacity. But if the spoon was plunged into a pot containing, for example, a thousand parts of water or broth, into which only a hundred parts of milk had mixed and blended in, and then a new (or not-within-its-day) spoon whose capacity equals a hundred parts was plunged in — although one estimates the spoon absorbed a quantity equal to its capacity (a hundred), not all of this hundred is milk, since it drew from the "shared pool" of water and milk together. Therefore one must calculate the proportional share belonging to the spoon from the milk alone, according to the ratio, and sixty is required only against that proportional share when the spoon later enters a meat pot. The Ben Ish Chai brings that the view of the authorities (the Chida in Shiyurei Berachah, citing Maharash Amar and others) supports this proportional calculation method, and so his grandfather Rabbi Moshe Chaim ruled, and so is the practice.

And should one ask: why not also consider the pot itself a "partner" in the broth — just as the broth drew from the milk, so too the pot absorbed proportionally? — the Ben Ish Chai discussed this question at length in his responsum in the book "Rav Pe'alim," analyzing the words of the authorities and clarifying the matter there.
takeaways: "Estimating against the spoon's entire capacity" applies specifically when plunged into milk alone; a spoon plunged into a pot of mixed water and milk requires calculating only its proportional share of milk absorbed, against which sixty is needed.
The proportional calculation method follows the Chida's view, citing Maharash Amar, and the tradition of the Ben Ish Chai's grandfather Rabbi Moshe Chaim, and is the accepted practice.
The question of whether the pot itself should also be considered a "partner" is discussed at length by the Ben Ish Chai in "Rav Pe'alim."

paragraphs: Im tachab kap cholebet biqdera shel basar al haesh shette peamim tzarik shette peamim shishshim, dechashebinan lah keillu tachab shette kappot: abal im tachab venoda denitbattel beshishshim, vechazar vetachab paam shenit, chozer umitbattel beotam shishshim, veap-al-gab dmvr"m za"l katab desaggi bechad shishshim,benitchab shette peamim anan batar maran za"l geriran, depasaq shetztzarik shette peamim shishshim. veim tachab oto yoter mishte peamim yesh soberim bedato shel maran za"l, disbira lah desaggi bishte peamim shishshim apillu im nitchab kamma peamim: veyesh soberim daat maran za"l, baenan shishshim keneged kol paam bipne atzmah. al-ken behepsed merubbeh, saggi bishte peamim shishshim keneged kol happeamim, yaan deikka sepeq-sepeqa bazeh, ubehepsed merubbeh abedinan sepeq-sepeqa kazeh lismok alayv, ap-al-gab desapeq haechad hu keneged maran za"l. veim hashshoel lo higgid lemoreh kamma peamim tachabu et hakkap: yesh omerim shetztzarik hammoreh lishol oto, veyesh omerim sheen tzarik hammoreh lishol: vaanachnu minhagenu shello lishol al zot, mishshum dibiqqar haddin sober mvr"m za"l udeimmah desaggi bepaam achat shishshim, apillu tachabu harbeh.

clarification.explanation: A dairy spoon plunged into a meat pot on the fire twice requires "sixty" twice (considered as though two spoons were plunged in). But if plunged once and it became known it was nullified in sixty, and it was then plunged in again, it is nullified again in that same sixty. And although the Rema wrote that one sixty suffices for two plungings, we (the Sephardim) follow Maran, who ruled that sixty is required twice. And if plunged in more than twice — some hold, in Maran's view, that sixty twice suffices even for several plungings, and some hold sixty is required against each plunging. Therefore, in a case of great loss, sixty twice against all the plungings suffices, since this involves a "double doubt" (even though one doubt is against Maran). And if the questioner did not tell the authority how many times the spoon was plunged — some say the authority must ask, and some say he need not; our custom is not to ask, since by the primary law the Rema and those who agree with him hold that even one sixty suffices for many plungings.
takeaways: A dairy spoon plunged twice into a meat pot requires sixty twice (following Maran, not the Rema, who is satisfied with one sixty).
Plunged more than twice — disputed in Maran's view; in great loss, sixty twice for all the plungings suffices (a double doubt).
Our custom is not to ask how many times it was plunged, since by primary law one sixty suffices.

paragraphs: Kap shel chalab shettechabo oto biqdera shel basar yesh omerim deen tzarik leshaer ella keneged mah shennitchab mimmennu betok hattabshil, abal cheleq shello niknas betok hattabshil, ap-al-pi shehu betok chalal haqqedera sheyyesh sham hebel, en tzarik leshaer kenegdo: veyesh omerim shetztzarik leshaer gam keneged hacheleq shebbetok chalal haqqedera: vesabera rishona iqqar: veken hamminhag pashut poh irenu bagdad, deen meshaarin ella keneged hannitchab betok hattabshil davqa. mihu, im hakkap hu shel matteket velekka hepsed merubbeh, meshaarin bekullo: dibmatteket amerinan: cham miqtzato cham kullo: abal i ikka hepsed merubbeh o sheat haddechaq, lah amerinan: cham miqtzato - cham kullo, leshaer keneged kullo, ella meshaarin keneged mah shennitchab battabshil davqa, yaan ki maran za"l satam besiman tzad, seip  kisbarat hammattirin, velo hebi sebarat haoserin ella beshem "yesh mi sheomer": veken bisip v lo zakar sebarat haoserin kelal, ubesiman tzch, seip g, achar shessatam kehammattirin, katab: yesh mi shemmachmir veku' , dehaynu lachush behepsed muat davqa.

clarification.explanation: A dairy spoon plunged into a meat pot — some say one need estimate only against the part that entered the dish, but not against the part in the pot's cavity (which holds vapor); and some say one must estimate against the cavity part too. The first view is primary, and so is the Baghdad custom — one estimates only against what was plunged into the dish. Nevertheless, if the spoon is metal and there is no great loss, one estimates against its entirety, since with metal one says "hot in one part is hot throughout"; but in a case of great loss or a pressing situation, this is not said, and one estimates only against what was plunged into the dish, since Maran ruled plainly according to the lenient view and cited the stricter view only as "some say" (to be concerned for only in minor loss).
takeaways: A dairy spoon in a meat pot — one estimates (sixty) only against the part that entered the dish (the Baghdad custom).
With a metal spoon and no great loss, one estimates against its entirety ("hot in part is hot throughout"); but in great loss or a pressing situation, only against the part plunged in.

paragraphs: Im omer hashshoel: bari lo, ad kan nitchab naamin lidbarayv, vela amerinan: kol milleta dela ramya alah deenash, lav addatah: vaapillu im ishsha omeret ken naamin lah: veken hamminhag pashut poh irenu.ubesipri haqqadosh "rab-pealim" heerakti beinyan zeh dekol milleta dela ramya alah deenash, bekamma inyanim shel dino issur vehetter,beinyanim sheyyesh lehistappeq bahem bedin zeh, uberarti besiyyata dishmayya kamma inyanim.

clarification.explanation: If the questioner says he is certain how much of the spoon entered the dish, his words are believed, and one does not say that since this is a matter a person usually does not pay attention to, he does not remember correctly. This law applies also if a woman is the one saying it — she is believed. And so is the accepted Baghdad custom.
takeaways: The questioner (even a woman) is believed when stating with certainty how much of the spoon entered the dish, even regarding a matter usually unnoticed.

paragraphs: Kap shel chalab shettechabo otah biqdera shel basar al haesh, veshier hammoreh sheyyesh shishshim battabshil shebbaqqedera lebattel hakkap hinneh, ap-al-gab dehaqqedera vehattabshil muttarim, mikkol maqom hakkap atzmo asur lehishtammesh bo ben im basar, ben im chalab lepi shehu belua mibbasar vechalab: vaapillu im shear debarim sheenam lo basar velo chalab, kegon orez vekayyotze, asur lehishtammesh bekap zo shenneesta nebela, utzerika hagala.

clarification.explanation: A dairy spoon plunged into a meat pot on the fire, where the authority determined there is sixty in the pot's dish to nullify it — although the pot and dish themselves are permitted, the spoon itself remains forbidden for use, whether with meat or with milk, since it is absorbed with both together and is considered like meat-and-milk (having become "nevelah" for this purpose). Even using it for things that are neither meat nor dairy (like rice) is forbidden, unless it is first purged.
takeaways: A spoon absorbed with meat and milk together, nullified in sixty — the spoon itself remains forbidden for use (with meat, milk, or even pareve) until purged.

paragraphs: Kol dabar habbalua baqqedera hen basar, hen chalab sheabar alayv esrim vearba shaot, have taam pagum, veeno asur min hattora: veraq chaza"l asaruhu lekattechilla ubediabad muttar. velaken qedera shebbishshel bah basar, veachar meet leet, dehaynu achar esrim vearba shaot, bishshel bah chalab, have lah noten taam lipgam,vehattabshil muttar, meachar shekkebar abar ubishshel dehave diabad: abal haqqedera atzmah, asur lebashshel bah lekattechilla, lo basar velo chalab, ella yagilenna, veachar hagala, muttar lebashshel bah mah sheyyirtzeh, veken hu haddin im kissa haqqedera shel habbasar bikli shel chalab sheeno ben yomo, deneesar hakkeli hazzeh: veasur lekassot bo lekattechilla, hen basar, hen chalab, ella tzarik sheyyagilennu. veim haqqedera shel habbasar shebbishshel bah chalab, o hakkissuy hazzeh shel chalab shekkissa bo haqqedera, hem kele-cheres en lahem taqqana shel me-raglayim: abal asur lehashhotam bebeto kemo shehem, gezera shemma yishkach veyishtammesh bahem mihu, im habbasar hu besar op deissuro midderabbanan, veikka hepsed merubbeh im yimkerennu legoy, kegon shehu keli chashub sheqqorin "pirpure"(cheres betzippuy matteket) yesh lehattir behepsed merubbeh, vaayin "chiqre - lb", yoreh dea, cheleq , siman ch, ushear acharonim. mihu, tzarik lehorot sheyyagilem shelosh peamim, kedin kol cheres beissur bishshule goyim, veken im hinnicha tabshil basar, apillu shel behema, bikli sheni shel chalab shehu keli "pirpure": veyesh hepsed merubbeh im yimkerennu legoy, muttar lehagilo shelosh peamim vedayyo: vehaynu davqa im hattabshil cham shehayyad soledet bo, abal im eno cham kol-kak, en tzarik hagala.

clarification.explanation: Any taste absorbed in a pot (whether meat or milk) over which twenty-four hours have passed is considered a "spoiled taste," and is not Torah-forbidden — the Sages forbade it only as the primary practice, but after the fact it is permitted. Therefore a pot in which meat was cooked, and only after twenty-four hours milk was cooked in it, is considered "imparting a spoiling taste," and the dish is permitted (since it has already happened after the fact). But the pot itself may not be used again as the primary practice to cook either meat or milk, unless it is first purged, after which it may be used as one wishes. The same law applies if a meat pot was covered with a dairy lid not within its day — the lid becomes forbidden, and may not be used as the primary practice, only after purging. Earthenware vessels forbidden this way have no remedy through soaking in urine, but it is forbidden to leave them at home as they are, out of concern one might forget and use them; unless it concerns fowl meat (whose prohibition is only rabbinic) and there is great loss (such as an expensive metal-plated vessel) — then it is permitted after a triple purging.
takeaways: A taste over which twenty-four hours passed ("imparting a spoiling taste") is not Torah-forbidden, so a resulting dish is permitted after the fact, but the vessel itself is forbidden as the primary practice until purged.
An earthenware vessel forbidden with fowl meat (a rabbinic prohibition), in a case of great loss, may be permitted through a triple purging.

paragraphs: Kissuy haqqedera, dino kiqdera atzmah: veap-al-gab deyesh machmirin bekissuy tepe, usebira lehu: apillu eno ben yomo, chashib keben yomo ledidan bene hasseparaddim, let lan chamra zo: vaayin "peri-chadash", seip h. mihu, im hakkissuy qatzar milmala, veyesh bo chalal shei epshar lehitqanneach yapeh, tzarik shishshim keneged maqom haqqatzar, ap-al-pi shehakkissuy eno ben yomo: vegam zeh yesh lehattir behepsed merubbeh o sheat haddechaq: veayyen "aruk-hashshulchan".

clarification.explanation: The law of a pot's lid is the same as the pot itself. Although some are stringent regarding a lid and hold that even if not within its day, it is treated stringently as though it were — the Sephardim are not stringent this way. But if the lid's shape has a narrow cavity difficult to clean thoroughly, sixty is required against that narrow spot, even if the lid is not within its day; and in a case of great loss or a pressing situation, one is lenient about this too.
takeaways: A pot's lid has the same law as the pot itself (no need to be more stringent with it); but a narrow, hard-to-clean cavity in it requires sixty against that spot.

paragraphs: Ap-al-pi sheamarnu: im abar ubishshel chalab biqdera shel basar sheenah bat-yoma, hattabshil muttar, haynu davqa biqdera mudachat uneqiyya, abal im haya shumman beayin tach al paneha, tzarik shishshim keneged oto hashshumman, ubistam, dela yadeinan im haya shumman tach al paneha o lav, amerinan: setam kelim hammutznaim, hem mudachim uneqiyyim, chutz min hassakkin, debistam amerinan: setam sakkin, shamnunit qarush aleha veraq i yadeinan beberur shehi neqiyya, az muttar.

clarification.explanation: The rule that a meat pot not within its day, in which milk was cooked by mistake, permits the dish, is true specifically when the pot is rinsed and clean. But if there was actual (visible) fat on the walls' surface, sixty is required against that fat. And when it is not known for certain whether there was fat on it, the assumption is that vessels stored in a cabinet (put away) are considered rinsed and clean — except for a knife, regarding which the assumption is that it has congealed grease on it, unless it is clearly known to be clean.
takeaways: The leniency of cooking milk in a meat pot not within its day depends on the pot being clean of visible fat; stored vessels are presumed clean, except a knife, presumed to have grease unless known to be clean.

paragraphs: Im bishshel biqdera sheenah bat-yoma debarim charipim,kegon hattabshil sherubbo chometz o tablin, veen shishshim lebattel: im yesh bazeh hepsed merubbeh,yesh lehattir kisbarat hammattirim desatam maran kevatayhu" veim hepsed muat, yesh lehachmir kisbarat hacholeqim, disbira lehu: en noten taam lipgam bidbarim hacharipim, dacharapyahu meshavve lah leshebach: yaan ki maran za"l zakar dibrehem beshem "yesh omerim", lekak yesh lachush ledibrehem behepsed muat. mihu haashkenazzim geriri batar hakraat mvr"m za"l, veoserin bidbarim hacharipim gam behepsed merubbeh. mihu eno niqra charip mishshum meat tablin o meat melach shennatan letabshil, ella im ken rubbo charip.

clarification.explanation: If sharp foods were cooked in a pot not within its day (such as a dish mostly of vinegar or sharp spices), and there is no sixty to nullify the previous taste — in a case of great loss, one may be lenient following the permitting view (which is the view of most authorities and Maran). But in a case of minor loss, it is proper to be stringent following the dissenting view, which holds that with sharp foods one does not say "imparting a spoiling taste," since the sharpness actually enhances the taste rather than spoiling it — since Maran cited this view only as "some say," and therefore one should be concerned for it when the loss is small. The Ashkenazim, following the Rema, are stringent with sharp foods even in a case of great loss. Something is not considered "sharp" merely due to a little spice or salt — only if most of the dish is sharp.
takeaways: In a pot not within its day with a sharp dish (without sixty): in great loss, be lenient; in minor loss, be stringent, since sharpness prevents "imparting a spoiling taste."
"Sharp" applies only if most of the dish is sharp, not due to minor seasoning.

paragraphs: Dagim o betzim veorez vekayyotze, shennitbashshelu biqdera shel basar neqiyya ap-al-pi shehaqqedera bat-yoma, muttar leekol et hambushshal hu bechalab, deen kan ella noten taam bar noten taam, demuttar lekattechilla. vekol zeh ledidan deazelinan batar horaat maran za"l, abal lehaashkenazzim deazeli batar mvr"m za"l, asur leekol hambushshal hahu bechalab lekattechilla, usebira lehu, eno muttar ella bediabad shekkebar natan et hambushshal hahu bechalab. vegam ledidan deazelinan batar maran za"l, eno muttar lebashshel lekattechilla biqdera shel basar bat-yoma addata dehaki, kede leokelam bechalab: ella raq im nitbashshelu bediabad muttar leakelam lekattechilla bechalab.velaken asur lechammem mayim lekattechilla bikle basar ben-yomo kede lalush bahem et happat, mippene dedarkam leekol happat im hechalab gam-ken. veken mirqachat sheddarkam leekol otah im haggebina, asur lebashshelah lekattechilla bikli basar ben-yomo.

Mihu im ken hakkeli ben-yomo, deikka tarte letebuta, shehu noten taam lipgam vegam noten taam bar notar taam, muttar lechammem mayim leepot happat, ulebashshel mirqachat leokelah im haggebina lekattechilla. ayyen "keneset haggedola" v"bet-david" ushear acharonim. vehammachmir shello lebashshel apillu bikli sheeno ben-yomo, tabo alayv beraka. veken nohagim bebetenu, sheyyesh lahem keli meyuchad lechammem bo mayim lalush bahem happat, veken lebashshel bo mirqachat. vaayin "debar-mosheh", yoreh dea, siman , v"chakemat-adam", kelal mch, seip b.

clarification.explanation: Fish, eggs, rice, and the like cooked in a clean meat pot, even within its day — it is permitted to eat this cooked food with milk, since this is "a taste imparted by a taste imparted" (a secondary, diluted taste) which is permitted as the primary practice. This follows Maran's ruling, but the Ashkenazim, following the Rema, forbid eating this with milk as the primary practice, permitting it only after the fact. Even according to Maran, it is forbidden as the primary practice to cook in a meat pot within its day with the explicit intent of eating the result with milk — only if this has already happened (after the fact) is it permitted. Therefore it is forbidden to heat water in a meat vessel within its day in order to knead dough with it, since some people eat bread with milk. Likewise, a preserve eaten with cheese may not be cooked as the primary practice in a meat vessel within its day. But if the vessel is not within its day (where there are two grounds for leniency: both "imparting a spoiling taste" and "a taste imparted by a taste imparted"), it is permitted to heat water in it and cook a preserve in it as the primary practice for eating with cheese. One who is stringent about this even with a vessel not within its day is praiseworthy.
takeaways: A pareve food (fish, eggs, rice) cooked in a meat pot within its day may be eaten with milk after the fact ("a taste imparted by a taste imparted"), but not cooked this way as the primary practice with that intent.
It is forbidden to cook in a meat vessel within its day something normally eaten with milk (like water for kneading bread, or a preserve with cheese) — unless the vessel is not within its day.

paragraphs: Im abar bemezid ubishshel lekattechilla orez o betzim vekayyotze biqdera shel basar bat yoma, al daat leakelam bechalab ap-al-gab daabad issura, la qanesinan lah, umuttar leokelam bechalab, vekannizkar b"peri chadash" ushear acharonim. veim debarim ellu shebbishshelam biqdera shel basar, nirgash bahem taam basar qiyyuha bealema ihu, vela chayeshinan lah, vekannizkar b"peri-chadash" u"bet-eprayim" siman lz, dap lb. mihu rsh"l za"l oser leakelam bechalab im nirgash bahem taam basar: ubaal-nepesh yachish lidbarayv, vehammeqel, yesh lo lismok.

clarification.explanation: If one deliberately and knowingly cooked rice, eggs, and the like in a meat pot within its day with the intent to eat them with milk — even though he committed a prohibition, he is not penalized, and it is nevertheless permitted to eat the food with milk. And if a slight meat taste is felt in these foods (a mere hint), there is no concern. However, there is a stringent opinion (the Rashal) forbidding eating them with milk if an actual meat taste is felt in them — one who wishes to be stringent may rely on this view, and the lenient view has authorities to rely upon.
takeaways: Deliberately cooking in a meat pot within its day, intending to eat with milk, is not penalized, and eating with milk is still permitted despite the transgression; if actual meat taste is felt, some are stringent.

paragraphs: Ha deamerinan "noten taam bar noten taam, muttar" - davqa taam harishon bakkeli vetaam sheni beokel, abal taam rishon beokel, la mehanne: debaokalim, apillu elep teamim chashubim kemammash. velaken im apu uga etzel pashtida shel chalab, asur leekol hauga hahi im habbasar, vela amerinan bazeh dehave noten taam bar noten taam: udelo keharab "pene-aryeh" shehebio b"pitche-teshuba". veayyen "keneset haggedola", siman tzh, haggahat habbet yosep, ot kv, ushear acharonim.

clarification.explanation: The rule "a taste imparted by a taste imparted is permitted" applies specifically when the first taste passed through a vessel, and the second taste passed to the food — but if the first taste was directly in the food (not in a vessel), the rule does not help, since with foods even a distant taste (even "a thousand tastes" removed) is considered as though actual. Therefore, if a cake was baked next to a dairy pastry (such that the cake absorbed dairy taste directly from the food), it is forbidden to eat this cake with meat, and one does not say "a taste imparted by a taste imparted" here, contrary to the view of Rabbi "Penei Aryeh" cited in "Pitchei Teshuvah."
takeaways: "A taste imparted by a taste imparted" helps only when the first taste passed through a vessel; a taste passed directly from food to food (like a cake baked next to a dairy pastry) is considered actual and forbids.

paragraphs: La amerinan noten taam bar noten taam, ella davqa behetter, kegon basar bechalab, sheshshenehem hemma min hetter: abal beissur, apillu kamma peamim noten taam bar noten taam, la mehanne: ella kol delekka shishshim lebattel haasur, hare zeh asur.

clarification.explanation: The rule "a taste imparted by a taste imparted is permitted" is stated only when both substances are permitted items (like meat and milk, each permitted on its own) — but when an actual forbidden substance is involved, even if it passed several times through "a taste imparted by a taste imparted," this does not help to permit it; rather, as long as there is no sixty to nullify the prohibition, the mixture remains forbidden.
takeaways: The leniency of "a taste imparted by a taste imparted" applies only between two permitted items (meat and milk); with an actual prohibition, it does not help — sixty is always required.

paragraphs: Qedera shel basar bat-yoma shebbishshelu bah orez vekayyotze, vetachab bah kap cholebet bat-yoma apillu en baorez shishshim keneged hakkap, muttar, dehave noten taam bar noten taam dehettera – dehabbasar natan taam baqqedera, vehaqqedera beorez, vaadayin hu hetter: mihu, tzarik sheyyihyeh barur lo dehakkap lo naga begup haqqedera - hen mitztzedadin shellah, hen beqarqaitah - deim naga begup haqqedera, en kan noten taam bar noten taam, dahare hakkap bala min haqqedera atzmah shehi taam echad. veken im tachab baorez shebbaqqedera shette kappot bene yoman, echad shel chalab veechad shel basar im lo nageu hakkappot zeh im zeh betok haorez, muttar hakkol. veayyen "chakemat adam", kelal mch, seip v. abal im nageu hakkappot zeh bazeh beet shettechabam baorez dehu roteach, hare hem boleim zeh mizzeh, veneesarim, veoserim haorez.

clarification.explanation: A meat pot within its day, in which rice and the like was cooked, into which a dairy spoon within its day was then plunged — even if there is no sixty in the rice against the spoon, it is permitted, since this is "a taste imparted by a taste imparted, both being permitted items": the meat imparted taste to the pot, and the pot imparted taste to the rice — and this is still considered a permitted taste. But one must clearly verify the spoon did not touch the pot's body directly (its walls or bottom), since if it did, the spoon absorbed a direct taste from the pot itself (a first taste, not a second), and this is no longer considered "a taste imparted by a taste imparted." Likewise, if two spoons — one dairy and one meat — were plunged simultaneously into the rice in the pot, and did not touch each other within the rice, everything is permitted. But if the spoons touched each other within the boiling rice, they absorb from each other and become forbidden, and forbid the rice too.
takeaways: A dairy spoon plunged into rice in a meat pot within its day (without sixty) is permitted, as "a taste imparted by a taste imparted," provided the spoon did not touch the pot's body directly.
Two spoons (meat and dairy) in the same rice are permitted if they did not touch each other; if they touched within the boiling rice, both become forbidden and forbid the rice too.

paragraphs: Setam kele goyim enam bene yoman: lepikak im abar ubishshel bikli shel goyim, hattabshil muttar bediabad, deamerinan en hakkeli ben–yomo, vehave noten taam lipgam. umikkol maqom lo yomar yisrael legoy: bashshel biqderateka mayim o chalab o shear perot, sheen bahem issur bishshule goyim dehave lekattechilla. al-ken asur lomar learbiyyim baale tzon sheyyaasu lo chalab chimmutz sheqqorin bearbi "laban", ubelaaz "ygvrty", ki zeh tzarik leharticho techilla, vehave lekattechilla: abal muttar liqnot mizzeh ha"yegoreti" min hashshuq poh irenu y", deen haggoyim osim oto bishbil yisrael, im haggoy makkir leyisrael, vehebi lo mincha keli acher mizzeh ha"yegureti" shemmebi limkor, muttar, mippene ki belav haki hu oseh hechalab shello kullo mizzeh ha"yegureti" kede lemakero.

clarification.explanation: Gentiles' vessels in general are presumed not to be within their day. Therefore, if one mistakenly cooked (transgressed and cooked) in a gentile's vessel, the dish is permitted after the fact, since the vessel is presumed not within its day and considered to impart a spoiling taste. Nevertheless, it is forbidden for a Jew to tell a gentile in advance, "cook in your pot," even water, milk, or fruit (things with no prohibition of gentile cooking), since this would be considered as the primary practice. Therefore it is forbidden to tell Arab flock owners to prepare sour milk (yogurt, called "laban") specifically for a Jew, since it must first be boiled, and this is considered the primary practice. But it is permitted to buy such yogurt from the market in Baghdad, since the gentiles do not produce it specifically for Jews; and even if a gentile personally knows a Jew and brings him a vessel of the yogurt he sells in the market as a gift, it is permitted, since he makes all his milk into this yogurt anyway to sell to everyone.
takeaways: Mistakenly cooking in a gentile's vessel is permitted after the fact (presumed not within its day); but it is forbidden to ask a gentile in advance to prepare a dairy product specifically for you.
It is permitted to buy yogurt from the market, and even as a personal gift from a gentile, since he produces it for the general public, not specifically for the Jew.

paragraphs: Keli shenneesar bibliat issur venitareb baacherim, batel berob – ben keli matteket, ben keli-cheres.

clarification.explanation: A vessel forbidden due to absorbing a prohibition, which afterward became mixed with other vessels (for example, in a large pile), is nullified in the majority — this law applies both to metal vessels and to earthenware vessels.
takeaways: A forbidden vessel later mixed with many other vessels is nullified in the majority, whether metal or earthenware.
